method: radar's default variant executed against eight real local clones, with and without --discount-common-path-keywords. Every number was measured by running the tool; none is estimated.
headline: At the default setting the report was unusable on openssl: 34.5% of a 400-commit window qualified. The cause was measured, not guessed -- sensitive_path fired on 132 of 138 candidates (96%), because the keyword 'crypto' matches 642 changed paths in that window: the entire project lives under crypto/. Discounting keywords that match most of the window takes openssl to 8.0% and leaves all seven other projects bit-identical, including every one of the 68 high-confidence findings.

discount_calibration.note: The two frequency marks bracket the measured gap. This is a calibration over eight projects, not a law: a project where a genuinely security-critical area occupies 30% of its commits will have that keyword ignored.

caveats: Candidate rate measures how noisy the report is at a given threshold. It is NOT an accuracy figure. It does not measure how many real silent fixes were found: recall cannot be computed from these runs because there are no ground-truth labels for silent fixes in the scanned windows, and no precision or recall claim is made anywhere in this file.
Removing 106 candidates removes unknowns, not known false positives. No manual review of the removed set was performed, so it is unknown whether any real silent fix was among them.
The discount is calibrated on eight projects and could be wrong for a project whose security-critical code legitimately dominates its history.

Parse timings on libtiff, openssl, redis and sqlite (244-435s for a 400-commit window) are inflated by the cache being cloned with --filter=blob:none, which fetches blobs on demand. Not a clean measurement of the tool; must be retaken on a full clone.
Six further planned projects were not fetched, so this is eight, not sixteen.
